rows.description: A visitor sees crowds push at temples, stations and matches, and notices most people are patient while a few cause chaos. Personal calm, awareness of exits and helping the vulnerable are wise habits.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child breaks a window while playing, hides in fear and then blames another child. Facing the neighbour with a parent and saying sorry teaches responsibility better than hiding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager hears a neighbour complain about music or cricket outside, and feels unfairly targeted. Both sides have rights; polite compromise on time and volume ends most disputes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult argues over a parking spot or a shared stairway and feels that giving in means being weak. Calm, fair talk, or the housing society's rules, settles things without lasting bitterness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young resident notices that a few people dominate a housing society meeting and others stay silent. Showing up, asking for written rules and speaking fairly help such groups work for all.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young person finds neighbours discussing their late hours, friends or marriage plans. Gossip stings; a steady, polite and open manner usually starves it more than defensiveness does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult greets neighbours, shares festival sweets and offers help in emergencies. A reservoir of goodwill makes conflicts easier to resolve and life safer.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An observer sees a small quarrel take on religious or caste colour as people take sides. Refusing to join the labelling, cooling talk and involving neutral elders help stop it spreading.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager posts and refreshes, feeling proud at likes and low at silence. Approval from strangers feels like worth, and adults can gently point out that numbers are not a measure of a person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, pride, detachment

rows.description: A teenager joins a viral dance or challenge to fit in, sometimes ignoring risk. Belonging is the real motive; a friend who says no thanks and stays friends shows that fitting in has options.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
